Activity per member

Source: R/context-anchor.R
member_activity.Rd

Counts each member's turns in v_speech, by parliament and chamber.

Usage

member_activity(
  PHID = NULL,
  parliament_id = NULL,
  chamber = NULL,
  chamber_venue = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  collect = TRUE,
  limit = NULL
)

Arguments

PHID

Character vector of member PHIDs. A PHID that matches no member is an error; look one up with find_member().

parliament_id

Filter on the sitting's parliament_id: whole numbers or in_range().

chamber

"house" and/or "senate", in any case.

chamber_venue

Filter on the turn's chamber_venue: whole numbers or in_range().

columns

Character vector of columns to return; NULL returns all.

collect

If TRUE (the default), return a tibble; if FALSE, a lazy table for further dplyr work.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return, or NULL for no limit.

Value

A tibble with one row per member, parliament and chamber in which the member had at least one turn or received an interjection, ordered by those three, and columns PHID, parliament_id, chamber, n_turns, n_speeches, n_questions, n_answers, n_interjections_made, n_interjections_received and n_words. Zero rows if nothing matches; a lazy table (in no set order) if collect = FALSE.

Details

Metrics. The three activity functions share these definitions:

  • n_turns: all turns in v_speech, including interjections. Quotes (action_type is "quote": passages read out, such as a letter or a petition) are not turns and are not counted by any metric.

  • n_speeches: turns with is_speech, is_question or is_answer set, and not is_interjection. This is the default of get_speeches(), so n_speeches equals the number of rows it returns for the same member and parliament.

  • n_questions, n_answers: turns with is_question (or is_answer) set that are not interjections.

  • n_interjections_made: turns with is_interjection set.

  • n_interjections_received: interjections in v_interjection_target whose target turn (the turn interrupted) was made by the member, counted in the target turn's parliament and chamber.

  • n_words: words summed over the n_speeches turns. A word is a run of non-whitespace characters: the turn's content is trimmed and split on \s+. The count is computed when the query runs, because the database has no word-count column. Stored content is counted as it is, so a turn whose content is "N/A" counts one word.

Grain and filters. parliament_id and chamber are the sitting's, from sittings. chamber_venue filters the turns (for received interjections, the target turns). Turns without a PHID are not counted: presiding officers, and unmatched, unknown, collective and non-member speakers (see get_speeches()).

See also

party_activity(), parliament_summary(), get_speeches()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
member_activity()
#> # A tibble: 311 × 10
#>    PHID  parliament_id chamber n_turns n_speeches n_questions n_answers
#>    <chr>         <int> <chr>     <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 009CW            40 house         1          1           0         0
#>  2 009D2            40 senate        2          2           0         0
#>  3 009MD             1 house        13         13           0        12
#>  4 00AKI            47 house         8          7           5         0
#>  5 00AMN            47 house         1          1           1         0
#>  6 00AMR            40 house         1          1           0         0
#>  7 00AMR            47 house         1          1           0         1
#>  8 00AMX            40 house         1          1           0         0
#>  9 00AN2            40 house         1          1           1         0
#> 10 00AN3            40 house         1          1           0         0
#> # ℹ 301 more rows
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: n_interjections_made <dbl>,
#> #   n_interjections_received <dbl>, n_words <dbl>
member_activity(PHID = "ZD4", columns = c("parliament_id", "n_speeches", "n_words"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   parliament_id n_speeches n_words
#>           <int>      <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1            36          0       0
#> 2            40          5    1606
db_disconnect()
